assertions.establishes: Routing selects a specialized path for the identified category, avoiding competing task instructions in one prompt. Running both paths is unnecessary when each input needs only one.
Independent required subtasks support parallel sectioning. Voting repeats one task; it does not cover three different required checks.
Voting gathers multiple attempts at the same task. Chaining introduces dependence, while sectioning distributes different subtasks.
Orchestrator-workers supports subtasks determined from the specific input. Adding or reordering fixed workers does not provide that decomposition.
An evaluator-optimizer loop uses actionable feedback to refine a candidate against stable criteria. The stated evidence supports iteration rather than unrelated reruns.
Agent and workflow patterns can be combined. Adaptive investigation can feed a deterministic gate that every deliverable must pass.
Additional orchestration must justify its cost and latency. Here it fails a binding limit while adding no measured benefit.
Routing requires accurate classification to select the appropriate specialized path; supplied metrics identify classification as the bottleneck.
A programmatic intermediate gate can stop an invalid outline before downstream generation. A prompt request alone does not enforce the transition.
An agent needs observations from tools or execution to assess progress. A proposed action is not evidence that the environment changed successfully.
A harness stopping condition bounds execution independently of model decisions. A blocker checkpoint allows human judgment instead of endless autonomous cycling.
Framework abstractions can hide the prompts and responses needed for debugging. Inspecting the underlying interactions reveals which assumption failed.
Subagents support specialized instructions for focused subtasks. Separate prompts avoid imposing unrelated procedures on every worker.
An AgentDefinition tools list restricts the subagent’s available tools. Naming or describing a role alone does not remove capabilities.
A non-fork subagent does not receive the parent’s conversation history. The delegation prompt must carry the specific facts needed for the subtask.
AgentDefinition.description tells the parent when to use the subagent. Its prompt governs the subagent’s behavior after selection.
Programmatic agent definitions take precedence over filesystem definitions with the same name. Maintaining both with divergent content can therefore obscure the effective configuration.
Depth1 prevents subagents spawning descendants; concurrency4 limits running subagents to four when the documented ultracode exception is inactive.
Resuming the containing session makes its subagent transcript available; the agent ID identifies the specific worker to continue. A role name alone does not select a past execution.
The Agent SDK provides the Claude Code loop and tools as a library. Direct Client SDK model calls leave loop orchestration to the application.
For languages other than Python and TypeScript, the documented bridge to the same loop is the CLI as a subprocess with print mode and JSON output.
The Messages API supplies direct model access for custom loops. A pre-built agent harness owns orchestration that this prototype needs to implement itself.
A session is the running agent instance within an environment. Agent and environment resources describe configuration rather than one specific task execution.
The SDK supervises a CLI subprocess that owns shell and filesystem state. Concurrency planning must account for those processes rather than treating the SDK as a stateless wrapper.
Working-directory artifacts need their own persistence strategy. A session identifier or transcript is not a durable copy of every generated file.
The hosted SDK needs outbound access to its model provider and any remote tools it uses. Local file access alone does not establish either connection.
Ephemeral sessions tie a container’s lifetime to one task. They fit one-off work whose results are exported before teardown.
Assistant messages occur throughout execution. The result message records the loop outcome, and its subtype distinguishes success from stopping on an error or limit.
The SDK’s turn limit bounds tool-use round trips. Short output or small logs do not bound how many times the loop executes.
In SDK default mode, uncovered tools go to canUseTool; without that callback they are denied. A headless embedding should not expect an interactive terminal prompt.
The SDK query budget includes subagent spend. Separate worker contexts do not create free or excluded model requests.
The Agent SDK executes requested tools and feeds their results back into its loop. Executing the same managed call again outside that loop duplicates the action.
ResultMessage marks the loop outcome, but a small number of system events can follow. Consuming the stream to completion preserves those events.
The compact boundary event identifies conversation compaction. It concerns context management, not file restoration, permissions, or model training.
Partial-message streaming adds raw events as generation proceeds. The app must extract text deltas rather than waiting for complete assistant messages.
Partial events are emitted in addition to complete assistant messages. Treating both as new text duplicates the same content.
Creating a session and sending its work are separate steps unless initial events are supplied. The task must be delivered as a user event.
A versioned agent reference pins which agent configuration the session runs. A bare ID selects the latest version.
Continue selects the most recent session in the directory; resume targets a specific session ID. Multi-session applications must select the intended authorized conversation explicitly.
Forking creates a separate conversation initialized from the original history. The original thread remains available under its own ID.
A session fork does not branch the filesystem. Separate working copies or another filesystem isolation strategy are needed to keep edits apart.
Cross-host continuity requires available state. You can retain transcripts for resumption or preserve the needed task state and seed a new conversation; an ID alone contains neither.
TypeScript persistSession: false keeps the session in memory for the call instead of writing its transcript. A fresh default session can still be persisted.
Checkpointing tracks designated file-editing tools, including Edit and Write. Bash changes and unrelated external side effects are outside that mechanism.
File rewinding restores tracked filesystem state while retaining conversation context. It is not a conversation fork or rollback of external actions.
A feature ledger makes remaining requirements visible across sessions. Visible progress on one part no longer substitutes for evidence that every required feature works.
Reading the handoff establishes intended recent work; exercising the current application checks the actual baseline. Neither a stale summary nor immediate new edits establishes both.
The documented long-running harness allows coding agents to change feature passes status while prohibiting removal or editing of acceptance tests; completion requires verification.
A coherent versioned increment plus explicit progress notes gives the next session a recoverable working state and task handoff. Unfinished undocumented work defeats both goals.
The requirement is about the distribution of complete-response latency. A 95th-percentile measurement tests that threshold; a mean or first-token measurement does not.
Recall on the urgent subset measures how many genuine urgent cases are caught. Overall accuracy and precision answer different questions and can conceal missed urgent tickets.
Success criteria should include operational constraints such as price and latency alongside task fidelity. Those are the two unmet requirements described in this pilot.
Task-specific evaluations should include edge cases such as nonexistent or irrelevant inputs. The application needs an explicit expected outcome for those cases before readiness can be measured.
Qualitative criteria become more repeatable when they use a defined scale and explicit rubric. Token counts and deployment size do not resolve what professional tone means.
Context utilization must be tested with cases that actually depend on earlier turns. Isolated questions cannot demonstrate that the assistant meets the follow-up requirement.

Inference budgeting needs expected input and output usage, request frequency, and the applicable model prices. The stem already provides volume and input measurements, leaving output usage and pricing.
Success criteria should be specific, measurable, relevant, and achievable. An undefined universal correctness promise cannot be validated; scope and evidence are needed before committing to a target.

Privacy criteria must specify the information and behavior being measured. Defined prohibited categories and a disclosure metric permit testing; disclaimers and answer length do not establish privacy preservation.
A held-out set tests task performance beyond the cases used for iteration. Reusing only the tuning examples cannot establish how the revised prompt behaves on unseen representative inputs.
Task-specific evaluations should cover real edge cases. Adding representative cases makes the discovered failure class part of future regression checks rather than a one-time demonstration.
Anthropic recommends testing the reliability of LLM-based grading before scaling. A defined rubric and reference judgments provide evidence that the automated scores measure the intended quality.
Message Batches target work that does not need immediate responses and can run until the batch expiration window. They are not a way to guarantee a ten-second interactive decision.
Batch result downloads have a limited retention period. Six-month application retention therefore requires storing the needed result artifacts outside that temporary download window.
Ended describes completion of batch processing, not universal success. Each request has its own outcome and must be handled accordingly.
Message Batches are limited by both request count and payload size, whichever is reached first. A submission must satisfy both limits; meeting just one does not make it valid.
Cancellation passes through canceling to ended and can leave partial successful results. Inspecting per-request outcomes preserves completed answers.
Requests in a Message Batch are processed independently. A batch is not a dependency graph that injects one result into another request.
Per-item Messages parameter validation occurs asynchronously. Testing request shapes with the Messages API and inspecting item results is necessary even after batch creation succeeds.
Batch requests do not support stream: true because results are delivered as a result file. Streaming that file during download is different from live token streaming within a batch item.
Creation returns a batch tracking object. The application must wait for processing to end and retrieve per-request results through the batch result interface.

A routing integration needs well-defined intent categories and an understanding of how the support team handles edge cases. Resolving service ownership provides the classification contract that prompt optimization must implement.

Evolving intent categories require updated definitions and evaluation examples. Capacity changes do not teach the router the new classification contract, and old-category coverage remains useful for regressions.

Task evaluations should reflect real usage, and the ticket-routing guide calls for measuring performance across languages. The original English-only result cannot establish quality for the changed traffic mix.
Deprecated models may still work, but retired models are unavailable and requests fail. Testing and migrating before retirement avoids making failure the migration trigger.

Anthropic distinguishes its operated-platform retirement dates from partner-operated schedules. A multi-provider maintenance plan must check the relevant provider dates rather than assume one universal deadline.
The model-deprecation guide describes exporting usage by API key and model to locate remaining usage. That inventory identifies migration scope across callers.
Content-block indices identify positions in the final content array, and delta types identify the field being updated. Separate typed accumulation preserves text and tool-input blocks.
Tool-input deltas are partial JSON strings. Accumulate the strings for the block and parse the completed input rather than requiring every fragment to be standalone JSON.
Usage token counts in message_delta events are cumulative. Summing successive totals double-counts earlier tokens.
content_block_stop ends one block, while message_stop ends the message stream. A response can contain multiple blocks before the final event.
Anthropic may add event types within a version and recommends handling unknown types gracefully. An informational extension should not be mistaken for text or a tool call.
Ping events can appear throughout a stream and do not represent answer content. They should not erase or be appended to the generated text.
Historical assistant messages can be synthetic. Including one supplies context; it does not create automatic server-side conversation memory.
The vision request shape uses a typed image content block with a source describing the encoded image. Plain text containing base64 is not that image-input representation.
The Messages vision interface accepts a URL source for an image block. This supplies the image directly without a local base64 conversion step.
For stop_reason stop_sequence, the response’s stop_sequence field identifies the matched sequence. Other metadata fields do not encode that match.
Direct requests must include anthropic-version; official SDKs normally supply it automatically. The API protocol version is separate from the model identifier.

The API versioning policy preserves existing parameters but permits additional output values and optional inputs. A consumer should not mistake an additive response field for a protocol-breaking change.
Each SDK invocation can make one initial attempt plus two retries. Three outer invocations can therefore produce nine HTTP attempts, so retry layers must be accounted for together.
Setting max_retries=0 disables the SDK’s automatic retries. A value of one permits an additional attempt, while timeout and output length do not establish retry ownership.
The Python SDK supports per-request overrides through with_options. That gives the background request its policy without changing the shared default used by other calls.
The Python SDK retries timed-out requests under its retry policy. A per-request timeout is not by itself a total wall-clock budget across attempts and backoff.
SDK list methods are paginated; iteration can fetch all pages, or callers can explicitly retrieve next pages.
with_raw_response exposes headers and its parse method returns the normal parsed response object.
with_streaming_response requires a context manager so the response is reliably closed.
Python SDK documentation shows model_fields_set for distinguishing missing fields from explicit null.
The Python response models provide to_json and to_dict serialization helpers.
The SDK sends the documented version header by default; overriding it may cause type mismatches and unexpected behavior.
extra_query, extra_body and extra_headers can override documented parameters of the same name and should use trusted input.
The async client accepts PathLike file uploads and reads their contents asynchronously.
Python numeric timeout values are expressed in seconds.
The Python async Messages example awaits a Message; persisted batch operations use the separate messages.batches interface.
The documentation recommends anthropic.__version__ to identify an older runtime version when upgraded features are missing.

A JSON serializer escapes quotation marks and control characters within string values while preserving their decoded content. Manual stripping changes the input, and double encoding changes the body type.
JSON object names should be unique for interoperable interpretation. Duplicate-name handling differs among parsers, so neither first-wins nor last-wins is a universal rule.
JSON objects and arrays have different ordering semantics: object-member order should not be relied upon, while arrays are ordered sequences. An adapter must preserve meaningful content-array order.
The JSON literal true is a boolean; quoted values are strings and 1 is a number. Type-sensitive consumers must receive the type the contract requires.
NaN and Infinity are not permitted by the standard JSON number grammar. The application needs an explicit valid representation or rejection policy for non-finite calculation results.
JSON numeric precision is limited by consumer implementations. A decimal string preserves an identifier’s digits when the receiving numeric type cannot represent them exactly.
Awaiting a coroutine provides its result for the dependent operation. Concurrency does not remove a data dependency or turn a coroutine object into its resolved value.
asyncio.gather returns successful results in the order of its input awaitables. Completion timing does not reorder that result list.
With return_exceptions=True, gather aggregates exceptions alongside returned values. The application must inspect those entries and distinguish failures from successful answers.
TaskGroup cancels remaining tasks when a member fails with a non-cancellation exception and waits for tasks on exit. That matches the stated structured failure behavior.
Python recommends cleanup in try/finally and generally propagating CancelledError after cleanup. Swallowing cancellation can interfere with structured concurrency and the caller’s stop request.
A shared semaphore limits concurrent entries to the outbound-call region. Releasing each acquired permit in cleanup, commonly with async with, ensures failures do not permanently reduce capacity.
HTTP does not generally guarantee POST is idempotent. Losing the response does not establish that the server did not apply the request, so a duplicate side effect is possible.
HTTP 202 means processing has been accepted but is not complete. The application needs the service’s completion mechanism before claiming the export succeeded.
HTTP 204 indicates successful fulfillment with no response content. A body parser must respect that status instead of requiring JSON where the contract provides none.
git revert records a new commit reversing an earlier patch. It preserves the existing history, unlike rewriting the branch to remove or amend the published commit.
git diff --cached compares the index with HEAD by default. Plain git diff shows unstaged changes, while git diff HEAD includes working-tree changes beyond the staged patch.
The three-dot diff compares the merge base of the branches with the feature tip. That isolates the feature’s changes since divergence instead of comparing two independently advanced tips.
Claude Code guidance recommends giving the agent checks it can run and showing evidence. Executable cases for both required behaviors verify the contract more directly than prose or patch size.
Deterministic adapter behavior can be tested against explicit expected structures. Generative variability does not excuse changes to a pure serialization contract.
For UI changes, Claude Code guidance recommends visual verification against the intended result. Rendering the affected viewport provides evidence for clipping that non-rendering unit tests do not.
PDF processing supplies page images together with extracted text, preserving visual evidence that a text-only extraction would discard.
PDF support requirements specify standard PDF with no passwords or encryption.
Binary .docx files are not supported directly in document blocks. Convert to a supported representation such as PDF; relabeling the same binary content is not conversion.
The Files API returns a file_id that can be referenced in later Messages requests without uploading the bytes again. The document reference still belongs in each request that needs it.
Uploaded files cannot be modified or renamed. Updating content requires a new upload; the application should switch its reference and retire the old file.
Files uploaded by the application are not downloadable through the Files API. Preserve originals separately if the product must return them later.
Files are accessible across the API workspace rather than scoped to an application user or conversation. Treat IDs as server-side references and enforce the user-to-file mapping.
File expiration is a lifecycle control, not a guaranteed-deletion control. Content becomes unavailable through the API, while limited retention and metadata visibility can continue.
Native citations currently reference text, and scan-only PDFs without extractable text are not citable. A verified text representation supplies citable content.
Citations interleave citation information with text output and are incompatible with structured output formatting in the same request. The documented result is a 400 error.
Citation metadata provides source locations and cited passages for checking an answer. The renderer must retain that association to support source inspection.
PDF citation page numbers are1-indexed with exclusive end page numbers.
Search-result blocks let an application provide its own retrieved content with source and title metadata for native citations.
Search-result citations reference whole content blocks. Splitting the same text into focused blocks gives the model finer citation boundaries.
If a tool_result contains search_result blocks, all its top-level content blocks must be search_result. Supporting text can be placed inside one result’s text content array.
Search-result citation settings must be consistent across a request. Enable citations on all results when the application wants them all available as cited evidence.
Structured outputs do not support external schema references. Resolve external definitions into a supported schema before sending it.

The SDK can remove unsupported constraints from the transmitted schema while retaining their descriptions, then validate responses against the original schema. That validation preserves the application’s numeric requirement.
Numerical constraints such as minimum and maximum are unsupported in the transmitted structured-output schema. A supported schema plus application validation preserves the business bounds.
JSON outputs and strict tool use address different surfaces and may be combined.
Structured outputs support required fields, basic string/null types, and union types via type arrays or anyOf.
Refusals return200 and may not match the schema because safety refusals take precedence.
String enum and const capitalization is not guaranteed; avoid values differing only in capitalization; applies to JSON outputs and strict tools.
Complexity limits apply to combined schemas; simplifying nesting/optional fields and splitting requests are documented mitigations.
Lookahead/lookbehind are unsupported; unsupported schema features can cause400.
JSON outputs return the schema-shaped response in the response text content block.
PHI must not appear in schema definitions; compiled schema caches do not receive the same PHI protections as prompt/response content.
The preset object’s append field adds instructions while preserving the Claude Code preset. A standalone custom string replaces the preset prompt.
An empty settingSources list excludes user, project, and local settings. It does not disable managed policy or global configuration and is not filesystem isolation.
Including project settings loads project CLAUDE.md context. The SDK’s cwd determines project-level discovery, allowing the CLI and SDK to share the maintained file.
CLAUDE.md sources are combined as context, not merged under a hard settings precedence rule. Conflicting instructions should be reconciled explicitly.
The Agent SDK’s plugin option accepts local directories. Download or check out remotely distributed plugins first, then provide the plugin root path.
Plugin skills use the plugin-name:skill-name namespace. Explicitly invoking /billing-audit:review disambiguates the intended skill.
The SDK plugin path points to the plugin root, the parent of the component directories and optional manifest directory.
The SDK may skip a missing plugin path without ending the session. Verify the local path and the initialization message’s plugins inventory before declaring the required capability ready.
Plugins bundle skills, hooks, agents, and MCP servers for reusable, versioned distribution across projects and teams.
Installed plugins run from their installed location. CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT provides the plugin root so bundled resources can be referenced portably.
Automatic installation uses npm ci --ignore-scripts for this lockfile. Dependencies requiring lifecycle-script builds need a separate supported setup path.
The installed plugin root is version-specific, whereas CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA is intended for persistent data that outlives a plugin version. Keep code and durable state in their appropriate locations.
The plugin manifest supports dependencies on other plugins, including supported version constraints. This differs from a plugin’s own language-package dependencies.
A userConfig field marked sensitive masks entry and stores the value through the documented secure credential storage path rather than ordinary settings.json values.
Lossy compression can introduce artifacts that make text hard to read. Inspect the actual submitted images rather than assuming they preserve the originals’ legibility.
Image object counts can be approximate, especially for many small objects. A product requiring exactness needs independent verification rather than relying on output formatting or confidence wording.
Project-local settings scope an override to one developer’s project. If the file is created manually, explicitly keep it out of version control.
List settings such as permissions.allow are combined across sources rather than resolved like a single scalar value.
The --settings option applies supported overrides for that session without changing saved settings files.
Claude Code settings files use strict JSON. Fix the syntax, then inspect settings-source status to confirm the repaired file loaded.
Shared project settings outrank user settings; list merge behavior is separate.
Relative CLAUDE.md imports resolve relative to the file containing the import, not the process working directory.
CLAUDE.md import parsing skips code spans and fenced code blocks. A code span preserves a literal @path mention without importing its content.
Managed settings enforce supported restrictions, while managed CLAUDE.md supplies behavioral guidance. Markdown instructions are not a hard enforcement layer.
Path-scoped rules load when Claude works with matching files. They keep specialized guidance from occupying every session’s context unconditionally.
Ancestor CLAUDE.md files load at launch; subdirectory files load on demand.
Auto memory toggle controls automatic notes; CLAUDE.md is separately authored instruction context.
/init analyzes the codebase and suggests improvements if CLAUDE.md exists.
/context shows loaded Memory files for confirming CLAUDE.md loading.
An SSE error can occur after HTTP 200 has been returned. Success accounting must include the stream outcome instead of treating headers or a partial delta as completed generation.
The request-id identifies the API request for support correlation, while the structured error type and message describe the failure category and details.
A 413 request_too_large indicates that request bytes exceed the endpoint limit. Diagnose the payload size rather than model output or instruction style.
The API’s error type values may expand over time. An integration should handle an unknown category through a safe generic error path while preserving its diagnostic information.
A 403 permission_error means the key lacks permission for the specified resource. Investigate resource authorization and organization/workspace access, rather than prompt generation behavior.
The counting endpoint takes a model and structured inputs including system content and tools; it estimates input tokens.
Current token-counting and migration docs describe a newer tokenizer and recommend recounting against the intended model.
Input, cache-read, and cache-creation token counts all contribute to the context window.
max_tokens is a hard limit on total output, including thinking, rather than a required generation length.
The context window is working memory distinct from the corpus used to train the model.
Thinking tokens are a subset of max_tokens and are billed as output when generated.
max_tokens is a hard limit on total output, including thinking, rather than a required generation length.
Effort is soft guidance; max_tokens is a hard total-output limit.
Effort affects response text, tool calls and arguments, and thinking when active; it works with thinking disabled.
Adaptive thinking evaluates each request and can produce a turn without a thinking block.
Adaptive thinking includes interleaving reasoning with tool use automatically.
Use effort before wording-sensitive steering, and measure quality, latency and token usage on representative workload cases.
Fast mode uses the same model weights and capabilities with premium pricing.
Fast-mode speed gains focus on output tokens per second rather than time to first token.
Fast mode illustrates provider-specific availability: availability on the direct API does not establish availability on every other integration.
Autoregressive pretraining predicts subsequent text given preceding context.
Anthropic demonstrated planning for later words in poetry despite sequential generation; this refutes the claimed necessary inability.
Few-shot examples steer output format and task behavior; documentation distinguishes context, examples and variable inputs.
Clear instructions must specify desired behavior and constraints rather than assume shared context.
Examples should be relevant and diverse to avoid unintended patterns.
Few-shot examples steer format and accuracy and should mirror the intended use case.
XML tags help disambiguate mixed instructions, context, examples, and variable inputs.
Long-context guidance places long documents near the top and queries at the end.
The role-prompting example uses a top-level system role and a user task message.
Output-format guidance recommends stating what to do rather than only what not to do.
Use sequential numbered steps when instruction order or completeness matters.
Providing motivation and context behind instructions supports more targeted behavior and generalization.
Starting with Claude4.6 final assistant prefill returns400; structured outputs are the migration for schema-constrained output.
Tool usage guidance distinguishes asking for suggested changes from explicit instructions to make edits.
Current prompting guidance recommends targeted tool-use instructions and removing over-prompting that causes tool overtriggering.
Prompt caching has no effect on output-token generation and caches input prefixes, not final answers.
The default five-minute cache lifetime refreshes on each use, measured from the request start.
The one-hour TTL is intended for reuse gaps beyond five minutes, including paused conversations, and has an additional write cost.
Shorter-than-minimum prompts are processed without caching and without an error; zero cache usage can reveal this.
Changing tool definitions invalidates the tools/system/messages cache hierarchy.
For concurrent requests, a cache entry is available only after the first response begins; waiting for that point supports subsequent hits.
input_tokens excludes cache-read and cache-creation tokens; total input is the sum of the three categories.
Prompt caching bills cache writes and cache hits at distinct prices; the stem supplies illustrative rates rather than asserting a universal current price.
Mixed TTLs require longer lifetimes to precede shorter lifetimes in the prompt.
Opus 4.7 and later, including Opus 5, default to omitted thinking display while blocks can still appear.
Opus 4.7 and later, including Opus 5, reject non-default temperature/top_p/top_k; the safe migration is to omit them.
Current token-counting and migration docs describe a newer tokenizer and recommend recounting against the intended model.
A custom fetch function may be passed to a client instead of replacing globalThis.fetch.
The TypeScript SDK does not validate requests against their static types at runtime and sends extra values as-is.
A stream returned by create with stream:true can be canceled by breaking the loop or calling stream.controller.abort().
create with stream:true returns an async iterable without accumulating a final message, unlike the stream helper.
TypeScript SDK logs are intended for debugging and their format and content may change between releases.
The configured SDK logLevel still filters messages when a custom logger is supplied.
The SDK supports runtime-specific proxy configuration through custom fetchOptions.
TypeScript timeout values are expressed in milliseconds.
The SDK versioning policy permits static-type-only incompatible changes in minor releases.
The EventSource interface receives server-sent events and has no general upstream send method.
RFC6455 defines two-way communication over an established WebSocket connection.
The official optimization guide recommends comparing cost per completed or solved task rather than per-token price.
Escalation policies must count failed initial attempts and require a reliable failure signal, with added latency on escalations.
Select models against the application requirements and evaluate difficult workload tails rather than relying only on typical cases.
The optimization guide recommends separate sessions for effort comparisons because mid-session effort changes invalidate caching and distort results.
The optimization guide notes that generated output is billed again as input when retained in later agent-loop requests.
Choosing a model requires evaluating capabilities needed by the application.
Select models against the application requirements and evaluate difficult workload tails rather than relying only on typical cases.
Model IDs from the 4.6 generation use dateless versioned naming and identify pinned model versions, unlike some earlier convenience aliases.
Just-in-time retrieval maintains lightweight identifiers and dynamically loads content through tools.
Structured notes persist outside context and are pulled back into the context window later.
Overaggressive compaction can lose critical information; tune on complex traces, maximizing recall before precision.
Hybrid context strategies retrieve some context up front for speed and explore further on demand.
Server-side context editing does not require synchronizing the client history with the edited prompt.
exclude_tools names tools whose uses and results should never be cleared.
Only tool results are cleared by default; clear_tool_inputs true also clears calls/parameters.
clear_at_least requires a minimum clearing amount; if unavailable no strategy application occurs; tool-result clearing invalidates affected cached prefixes.
pause_after_compaction returns stop_reason compaction and permits adding content before continuing; compaction blocks must be passed back.
Custom summarization instructions completely replace the default prompt.
The token-counting endpoint applies existing compaction blocks but does not trigger new compactions.
Direct quote extraction before analysis grounds long-document tasks; external-knowledge restrictions and critical validation are recommended.
Explicit permission to admit uncertainty and restrict claims to supplied sources reduces hallucinations.
Citation verification may require finding a supporting quote for each claim and retracting unsupported claims.
Before prompt engineering establish clear success criteria, empirical tests, and an initial prompt.
Current mitigation guidance places third-party content in tool_result, not system or plain user text, and identifies provenance.
Do not put own instructions in tool results; send them in a user turn following the result.
Indirect injection includes adversarial instructions in OCR, emails, documents and tool results when the user is trusted.
Tool output screening occurs before returning content; flagged injection content is replaced by error or stripped summary.
Red-team workflows with documents/emails/tool results containing attacks and confirm screening and confirmation steps catch them.
Regularly analyze outputs for injection and iteratively refine prompts, validation and filters; red-team workflows.
Authorization URL validation requires rejecting dangerous schemes; production usesHTTPS; clients must avoid shell execution when opening URLs.
MCP security guidance recommends validating redirect targets and blocking private/reserved destinations including metadata addresses.
MCP servers MUST NOT use sessions for authentication and authorized servers MUST verify all inbound requests.
One-click local configuration MUST show exact untruncated command, identify code execution risk, require approval, and allow cancellation.
Bind session IDs to user-specific information; combine user_id and session_id with user identity derived from token.
Avoid unnecessary proprietary details; no prompt-leak mitigation is foolproof.
Leak prevention can degrade task performance; test prompts thoroughly and try monitoring/output screening first.
Effective sandboxing requires filesystem and network isolation; missing either leaves compromise routes.
Sandbox restrictions are OS-enforced on Bash and child processes regardless of model choice or command-name appearance.
Sandbox applies only to Bash commands and child processes; permission rules apply across tools.
PreToolUse does not fire for @ file references; use Read deny rules to block specific paths.
Multiple PreToolUse decisions have deny precedence over defer,ask,allow.
Browser support is disabled to avoid exposing secret credentials; dangerouslyAllowBrowser explicitly enables it.
Do not share API keys in public discussions, emails, or support tickets, even with Anthropic.
Ignore local dotenv files; prefer encrypted cloud secret storage and environment injection.
Regularly review logs and API key usage patterns within the Console.
MCP servers must validate intended audience, reject tokens not intended for them, and must not pass received tokens through to upstream APIs.
Tool descriptions should explain parameter meanings and behavior.
Invalid input_examples return 400; each example must satisfy input_schema.
tool_choice none prevents tool use; auto allows model choice.
On supported configurations, tool_choice tool forces a named tool while any permits any provided tool.
input_schema uses JSON Schema properties and required for parameter contracts.
Natural language commentary varies; structured tool_use blocks contain name and input.
Tool results must immediately follow calls and precede text in the user content array.
tool_use id uniquely identifies the call and tool_use_id correlates its result.
Applications choose concurrent or sequential execution; shared-state/ordering requirements favor sequential handling.
Skipped custom tool calls still receive their own error result with a brief explanation.
Independent read-only operations can run concurrently; return one result per call together.
Tools should perform targeted searches instead of dumping complete collections into model context.
Tool responses should expose useful semantic information and identifiers needed for later actions.
Client must send initialized notification after successful initialization.
stdio stdout must contain only valid MCP messages; stderr may carry diagnostics.
resources/subscribe registers URI interest; resources/updated notifies content changes.
prompts/get retrieves a named prompt with arguments.
Business and validation failures use tool-result isError; malformed/unknown operations are protocol errors.
Servers must return structured results conforming to outputSchema; clients should validate them.
Skills provide reusable instructions; MCP provides external tools and access; they compose.
Custom tools can run in an SDK in-process MCP server.
Register custom tools by passing their server to mcpServers; allowedTools preapproves registered tools.
API code execution sandbox disables internet/outbound network access.
Supporting skill files enable detailed reference material to load only when needed.
Local !command dynamic context executes before skill content is sent; output replaces placeholder.
Skill frontmatter opening --- must be the first line; otherwise entire file is content.
disable-model-invocation prevents model invocation while retaining explicit user invocation.
$ARGUMENTS supplies invocation arguments within skill content.
Skill allowed-tools grants permission and does not restrict availability of unlisted tools.
Existing .claude/commands files continue to work; skills add supporting-file structure.
Web fetch does not support JavaScript-rendered sites; interactive browser access is a different capability.
